newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND SHOW NO SIGN OF WAKING FROM NIGHTMARE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND SHOW NO SIGN OF WAKING FROM NIGHTMARE.

text.p: England skipper Mike Atherton's nightmare tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand continued on Saturday when he scored a duck and faced probable defeat against New Zealand A.
At the end of the third day of the four-day match, England, requiring 363 to win, were 166 for six, with Jack Russell on 19 and Robert Croft on 16.
Left-arm seamer Geoff Allott celebrated his recall to the New Zealand team for next week's second test by again knocking the top off the England innings, just as he had in the first innings.

Bowling with aggression, he dismissed openers Atherton and Nick Knight for four to have England reeling at six for two and returned later to have John Crawley caught behind and then bowled all-rounder Ronnie Irani.
Allott, who took four for 44 in the first innings, had four for 57 by stumps.
The only partnership of note had come from Nasser Hussain, who hit an impressive 57, and Crawley, who made 38 in 34 balls. They added 66 in 70 balls for the third wicket.

A win by New Zealand A would pile further shame on the England team. They have been lambasted by the England media for failing to beat lowly Zimbabwe in the tests and losing the one day series there as well as losing by seven wickets to Mashonaland.

Then, earlier this week, they had New Zealand on the ropes in the first test but allowed a record 10th wicket stand by Nathan Astle and the world record holder for test ducks, Danny Morrison, to thwart them.
